vendor: Engineering in the Age of AI (eai-org)
tagline: Refine → Plan → Act → Consolidate: a fresh session per phase, handing over a file.
bestFor: Ticket-driven work with a human reviewing each step
keyFeatures: Each phase runs in a fresh session and hands over a file, not chat history: `TICKET.md` → `REQUIREMENTS.md` → `PLAN.md` → `HANDOVER.md`
`/refine-ticket` checks the ticket against the code and interviews you one question at a time; `/create-implementation-plan` settles technical decisions and writes a self-contained plan
Optional `/harden-artifact`: a fresh-context reviewer tests a requirements doc or plan, then your session tries to disprove each finding
`/split-plan-tasks` and `/execute-plan-tasks` run one small task per session and stop for your review; the skill never commits, pushes, or opens a PR
Consolidate: `/fresh-eyes-review` by a fresh-context sub-agent, then `/handover` writes a paste-ready PR description

Adjacent to SDD rather than spec-driven: the ten workflow skills are part of a general 30-skill agent toolkit, and the README never uses the term spec-driven (our reading of the README and skill list)
Installs by symlinking skills into `~/.agents/skills` and the agent's own directory (`--skills-dir`); works with Claude Code, GitHub Copilot, Codex, OpenCode, and others
limitations: A skill collection, not a framework: nothing enforces the flow, and each phase is invoked by hand
Fresh context depends on you: each phase and each task needs a new session opened by hand
Requirements and plans are per-task working files, with no maintained living spec
No worktree isolation or parallel multi-agent orchestration
No hotfix path: the interview and handoffs are slow when production is down
Young project with no tagged releases (~108 stars, 20 forks, created 2026-05-25; figures as of 2026-11-21)
Submitted by an agent-toolkit contributor (PR #80, disclosed); scores are this repository's, assessed 2026-11-21 from the repository and docs, not from hands-on use
